description: This map supplies the three role views, the staff, the diagnoses and the drugs, with the translations of the drug and unit codes, from the invented catalogue, and it follows the existing invented conversion wherever that affects the neonatal audit, so that the two answers can be compared.

rows.from: PERSON_MASTER, which the team's queries read by PERSON_KEY
rows.says: One row of the patient table is one patient, and the key is unique in the stand-in database.
rows.question: Please confirm whether the patient table holds exactly one row for each patient, with no merged or duplicate records.

patient_key.says: The team's queries join the patient table to visits and theatre cases on this key.
patient_key.question: Please confirm whether PERSON_KEY is the key that visits and theatre cases carry for the patient.

birth_date.says: The birth time is cut to its date, so that the age in days counts calendar dates as the conversion does.
birth_date.question: Please confirm whether BIRTH_TS holds the date of birth, and whether it is ever the date of arrival rather than of birth.

death_date.says: The date of death comes from the second patient table, as the conversion's death step takes it.
death_date.question: Please confirm whether PERSON_MASTER_2.DEATH_TS records every death that the hospital knows of, including deaths after discharge.

is_test.says: A patient flagged Y is a test patient, and the team's queries leave such patients out.
is_test.question: Please confirm whether the flag marks every test and training patient in every year.

rows.says: One anaesthetic record is one anaesthetic, kept where its theatre case reaches a hospital visit with an admission time, as the conversion keeps it.
rows.question: Please confirm whether every anaesthetic has a theatre case, and whether an anaesthetic whose visit lacks an admission time should still count.

anaesthetic_key.says: The team's queries join the anaesthetic record to its observation sheets on this key.
anaesthetic_key.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_KEY identifies one anaesthetic, and whether a record can be listed twice.

patient_key.says: The patient is the hospital visit's patient, which the team's queries reach through the theatre case.
patient_key.question: Please confirm whether the visit's patient is always the patient of the anaesthetic, including for a newborn with a second record.

start_time.says: The start is the recorded start of the anaesthetic, in local time.
start_time.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_START_TS marks the start of anaesthesia, and not the time at which the record was opened.

stop_time.says: The stop is the recorded stop, and it is empty where none was recorded.
stop_time.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_STOP_TS marks the end of anaesthesia, and what an empty stop means.

rows.says: A reading on an observation sheet that carries an anaesthetic's key belongs to that anaesthetic, as the team's queries take it.
rows.question: Please confirm whether every reading charted during an anaesthetic is on a sheet that carries its key, in every year.

anaesthetic_key.says: The sheet carries the key of the anaesthetic that it was charted for.
anaesthetic_key.question: Please confirm whether OBS_SHEET.ANAES_KEY has been filled since the earliest records.

kind.says: The observation type says what was measured, and the kinds below give the codes of the two means.
kind.question: Please confirm whether any other observation type has ever held a mean arterial pressure.

reading_time.says: The reading time is the time at which the value was taken, in local time.
reading_time.question: Please confirm whether READ_TS is the time of measurement rather than the time of filing, in local time in every year.

value.says: The value is read as a number where it is one, rounded to three places as the conversion rounds it.
value.question: Please confirm whether READ_VALUE holds the mean in mmHg for both observation types.

accepted.says: A reading flagged N was not accepted, and an empty flag counts as accepted, as the team's queries treat it.
accepted.question: Please confirm whether an empty ACCEPTED_FLAG means that the value was accepted.

reading_key.says: A reading has no key of one column, so the map makes one value from the sheet and the line on it, which together identify a row.
reading_key.question: Please confirm whether the sheet and the line together identify one reading, with no line repeated on a sheet.

value_text.says: The value as charted is kept as text where it cannot be read as a number, and left empty where it is a number.
value_text.question: Please confirm whether READ_VALUE holds words as well as numbers, such as a note that a reading was not taken.

rows.says: One line of the anaesthetic's staff list is one period in which one person took part, so that a handover gives two lines.
rows.question: Please confirm whether the staff list records every person present, including the surgeon and the anaesthetic assistant, and whether a line can repeat.

anaesthetic_key.says: The staff list carries the key of the anaesthetic record.
anaesthetic_key.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_STAFF.ANAES_KEY is always filled.

person_key.says: The staff key points at the list of staff, and the view gives the key and never the name.
person_key.question: Please confirm whether one person keeps the same STAFF_KEY across the years.

role.says: The team's handover query reads only the staff role 1, which the map takes to be the anaesthetist, and the other roles are other until their meaning is known.
role.question: Please confirm whether the staff role 1 is the anaesthetist, and say what the roles 2 and 3 mean.

grade.says: The invented world records no grade for a member of staff, so the view gives it empty.
grade.question: Please confirm whether the list of staff, or any other table, records a grade.

present_from.says: The start is the time at which the person took over the care of the patient.
present_from.question: Please confirm whether START_TS is in local time.

present_to.says: The end is the time at which the person handed over the care of the patient.
present_to.question: Please confirm whether an empty END_TS means that the person stayed until the end of the anaesthetic.

rows.says: One line of a visit's diagnoses is one coded diagnosis of that stay, identified by the visit and the line.
rows.question: Please confirm whether the visit's diagnoses are those coded at discharge, and whether a code can appear twice for one visit.

diagnosis_key.says: A diagnosis is identified by the visit and its line in the visit's diagnoses, joined into one value.
diagnosis_key.question: Please confirm whether the visit and the line together identify one diagnosis row.

patient_key.says: The patient is the patient of the visit for which the diagnosis was recorded.
patient_key.question: Please confirm whether every visit carries its patient.

stay_key.says: The diagnosis carries the key of the hospital visit, which is the stay.
stay_key.question: Please confirm whether VISIT_DIAGNOSIS.VISIT_KEY is the same key that role_stay gives.

diagnosis.says: The diagnosis is the visit's code in the list of diagnoses, which the hospital schema has not yet translated into standard concepts, so the view gives it as the key unlisted.
diagnosis.question: Please confirm whether the list of diagnoses holds the codes that should be translated into standard concepts.

is_principal.says: A diagnosis flagged Y is the principal diagnosis of the visit, and one flagged N is another.
is_principal.question: Please confirm whether exactly one diagnosis of each visit is flagged Y.

recorded_time.says: The invented world records no time at which a diagnosis was noted or coded, so the view gives it empty.
recorded_time.question: Please confirm whether any table records when a diagnosis was coded.

source_kind.says: The visit's diagnoses are coded after the stay, so every row is of the source kind coded_record.
source_kind.question: Please confirm whether the visit's diagnoses are coded at discharge rather than taken from a problem list or a booking.

documented_time.says: The invented world records no time at which a diagnosis was entered, so the view gives it empty.
documented_time.question: Please confirm whether any table records when a diagnosis was entered.

amends_key.says: The invented world records no correction of a diagnosis as a row of its own, so the view gives it empty.
amends_key.question: Please confirm whether a corrected diagnosis is ever recorded as a row of its own.

rows.from: DRUG_GIVEN, the rows that amend no earlier row
rows.says: One administration row is one action of a drug given during an anaesthetic or the stay, as charted.
rows.question: Please confirm whether the administration table records every dose and every infusion action charted during an anaesthetic.

drug_event_key.says: The key is the administration row's own key, written after the word given so that it never meets the key of an order.
drug_event_key.question: Please confirm whether GIVEN_KEY is unique to each administration row, the corrections included.

anaesthetic_key.says: The administration row carries the key of the anaesthetic record during which the drug was given.
anaesthetic_key.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_KEY is filled for every drug given during an anaesthetic, and empty only for a drug given elsewhere in the stay.

stay_key.says: The administration row carries the key of the hospital visit, which is the stay.
stay_key.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_GIVEN.VISIT_KEY is the same key that the visits table holds.

order_key.says: The administration row carries the key of the order that it carries out, so that the actions of one infusion can be told from those of another.
order_key.question: Please confirm whether every action of one infusion carries the same ORDER_KEY, and whether a new bag starts a new order.

drug.from: the hospital schema's translation of DRUG_KEY into map_drug_concept
drug.says: The drug is the opaque key of the code in DRUG_KEY, and a code that the translation does not list gives the key unlisted.
drug.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_KEY names the drug given, rather than the product or the bag.

action.says: The action codes 1, 6, 10, 7, 9 and 8 are a dose given and an infusion started, changed in rate, paused, restarted and stopped, and any other code gives no action.
action.question: Please confirm whether each action code means what the map takes it to mean, and whether any other code has been used in any year.

amount.says: The amount is the dose, or the rate of an infusion, as charted, and it is empty on a pause or a stop.
amount.question: Please confirm whether DOSE_AMT holds the rate of an infusion in the unit beside it, rather than a volume.

unit.from: the hospital schema's translation of DOSE_UNIT_CAT into map_unit_concept
unit.says: The unit is the opaque key of the code in DOSE_UNIT_CAT, and a code that the translation does not list gives the key unlisted.
unit.question: Please confirm whether DOSE_UNIT_CAT is the unit of DOSE_AMT on every row.

route.says: The route codes 1, 2 and 3 are intravenous, oral and inhaled, as the conversion's route rows name them, and any other code, or none, is other.
route.question: Please confirm whether the route codes 1, 2 and 3 are intravenous, oral and inhaled, and say what the other codes mean.

given_time.says: The time given is the time at which the action took place, as charted, and a correction keeps the time of the action it corrects.
given_time.question: Please confirm whether GIVEN_TS is the time of the action rather than the time of filing, in local time in every year.

source_kind.says: A row that amends no earlier row is a record that the drug was given, so every row of this pathway is of the source kind administration.
source_kind.question: Please confirm whether every administration row records an action that was carried out, and not one that was planned.

documented_time.says: The time documented is the time at which the row was filed, which the hospital records apart from the time of the action.
documented_time.question: Please confirm whether DOC_TS is the time of filing, and whether a late entry keeps the time of the action in GIVEN_TS.

amends_key.says: An administration amends no earlier row, so the view gives the row it amends empty.
amends_key.question: Please confirm whether AMENDS_KEY always names a row of DRUG_GIVEN, and whether a correction can itself be corrected.

rows.from: DRUG_GIVEN, the rows that name the row they amend
rows.says: A row that names in AMENDS_KEY the row it amends is a retrospective correction of that row, and it gives the action, time and amount as corrected.
rows.question: Please confirm whether a correction is always charted as a row of its own that names the row it amends.

drug_event_key.says: The key is the administration row's own key, written after the word given so that it never meets the key of an order.
drug_event_key.question: Please confirm whether GIVEN_KEY is unique to each administration row, the corrections included.

anaesthetic_key.says: The administration row carries the key of the anaesthetic record during which the drug was given.
anaesthetic_key.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_KEY is filled for every drug given during an anaesthetic, and empty only for a drug given elsewhere in the stay.

stay_key.says: The administration row carries the key of the hospital visit, which is the stay.
stay_key.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_GIVEN.VISIT_KEY is the same key that the visits table holds.

order_key.says: The administration row carries the key of the order that it carries out, so that the actions of one infusion can be told from those of another.
order_key.question: Please confirm whether every action of one infusion carries the same ORDER_KEY, and whether a new bag starts a new order.

drug.from: the hospital schema's translation of DRUG_KEY into map_drug_concept
drug.says: The drug is the opaque key of the code in DRUG_KEY, and a code that the translation does not list gives the key unlisted.
drug.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_KEY names the drug given, rather than the product or the bag.

action.says: The action codes 1, 6, 10, 7, 9 and 8 are a dose given and an infusion started, changed in rate, paused, restarted and stopped, and any other code gives no action.
action.question: Please confirm whether each action code means what the map takes it to mean, and whether any other code has been used in any year.

amount.says: The amount is the dose, or the rate of an infusion, as charted, and it is empty on a pause or a stop.
amount.question: Please confirm whether DOSE_AMT holds the rate of an infusion in the unit beside it, rather than a volume.

unit.from: the hospital schema's translation of DOSE_UNIT_CAT into map_unit_concept
unit.says: The unit is the opaque key of the code in DOSE_UNIT_CAT, and a code that the translation does not list gives the key unlisted.
unit.question: Please confirm whether DOSE_UNIT_CAT is the unit of DOSE_AMT on every row.

route.says: The route codes 1, 2 and 3 are intravenous, oral and inhaled, as the conversion's route rows name them, and any other code, or none, is other.
route.question: Please confirm whether the route codes 1, 2 and 3 are intravenous, oral and inhaled, and say what the other codes mean.

given_time.says: The time given is the time at which the action took place, as charted, and a correction keeps the time of the action it corrects.
given_time.question: Please confirm whether GIVEN_TS is the time of the action rather than the time of filing, in local time in every year.

source_kind.says: A row that names the row it amends is a correction, so every row of this pathway is of the source kind correction.
source_kind.question: Please confirm whether a row with AMENDS_KEY filled is always a correction of the row it names.

documented_time.says: The time documented is the time at which the row was filed, which the hospital records apart from the time of the action.
documented_time.question: Please confirm whether DOC_TS is the time of filing, and whether a late entry keeps the time of the action in GIVEN_TS.

amends_key.says: A correction names in AMENDS_KEY the administration row that it amends, written in the same form as the key.
amends_key.question: Please confirm whether AMENDS_KEY always names a row of DRUG_GIVEN, and whether a correction can itself be corrected.

rows.says: One row of the order table is one order of a drug, written before it is given.
rows.question: Please confirm whether every infusion given during an anaesthetic has a row in the order table.

drug_event_key.says: The key is the order's own key, written after the word order so that it never meets the key of an administration.
drug_event_key.question: Please confirm whether ORDER_KEY is unique to each order.

anaesthetic_key.says: The order carries the key of the anaesthetic record for which it was written.
anaesthetic_key.question: Please confirm whether ANAES_KEY is filled for every order written during an anaesthetic.

stay_key.says: The order carries the key of the hospital visit, which is the stay.
stay_key.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_ORDER.VISIT_KEY is the same key that the visits table holds.

order_key.says: The order's own key is the key that its administrations carry.
order_key.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_GIVEN.ORDER_KEY always names a row of DRUG_ORDER.

drug.from: the hospital schema's translation of DRUG_ORDER.DRUG_KEY into map_drug_concept
drug.says: The drug is the opaque key of the code that the order names, and a code that the translation does not list gives the key unlisted.
drug.question: Please confirm whether the order names the same drug codes as the administrations.

action.says: Every row of the order table is an order, so its action is ordered.
action.question: Please confirm whether the order table holds only orders, and not doses already given.

amount.says: The amount is the dose or the rate that was ordered.
amount.question: Please confirm whether DRUG_ORDER.DOSE_AMT is the ordered dose or rate in the unit beside it.

unit.from: the hospital schema's translation of DRUG_ORDER.DOSE_UNIT_CAT into map_unit_concept
unit.says: The unit is the opaque key of the order's unit code, and a code that the translation does not list gives the key unlisted.
unit.question: Please confirm whether the order's unit codes are those of the administrations.

route.says: The route codes 1, 2 and 3 are intravenous, oral and inhaled, as the conversion's route rows name them, and any other code, or none, is other.
route.question: Please confirm whether the route codes 1, 2 and 3 are intravenous, oral and inhaled, and say what the other codes mean.

given_time.says: The time of an order is the time at which it was written.
given_time.question: Please confirm whether ORDER_TS is the time at which the order was written, rather than the time for which it was due.

source_kind.says: Every row of the order table is an order, made before anything is given, so it is of the source kind order.
source_kind.question: Please confirm whether every row of the order table is an order.

documented_time.says: The invented hospital records no filing time on an order apart from the time it was written, so the view gives it empty.
documented_time.question: Please confirm whether any table records when an order was filed.

amends_key.says: The invented hospital records no correction of an order as a row of its own, so the view gives it empty.
amends_key.question: Please confirm whether a changed order is recorded as a new row that names the order it replaces.

rows.description: Opioid infusion of the ward's own make
Opioid infusion of the ward's own make

map_arterial.from: OBS_TYPE_DEF and the conversion's mapping rows
map_arterial.says: The observation type 52 is the mean blood pressure from an arterial line.
map_arterial.question: Please confirm whether observation type 52 is the arterial mean, and whether it has held any other channel.

map_cuff.from: OBS_TYPE_DEF and the conversion's mapping rows
map_cuff.says: The observation type 51 is the mean blood pressure from the cuff.
map_cuff.question: Please confirm whether observation type 51 is the cuff mean as the monitor measured it, and not a mean calculated from a charted pressure.

eras.note: Nothing is yet known of a change over the years in how readings are filed, and the counts by year will show one if it exists.

questions.question: Please confirm whether deaths outside the hospital reach the second patient table, and how long after the death they arrive.
